description: Initial frozen benchmark produced a valid timing baseline, but benchmark type checking rejected accumulator inference in the 2D locate driver.

asi.hypothesis: A balanced, core-pinned compiled benchmark can establish stable baseline timings for the target Numba call patterns.
asi.rollback_reason: The benchmark's interp2d_locate return was inferred by ty as scalar-or-array, making the accumulator's inferred type incompatible with the annotated float return.
asi.next_action_hint: Restructure the benchmark-only 2D locate accumulator to explicitly read scalar buffer elements without rebinding from the overloaded public return, then rerun baseline.

description: Baseline verification after avoiding 2D locate return rebinding; benchmark ran correctly, but ty exposed the same public return-union inference for 2D evaluation.

asi.hypothesis: Ignoring the scalar locate return and consuming explicit output buffers would resolve the benchmark-only type ambiguity.
asi.rollback_reason: The locate ambiguity was resolved, but ty now inferred interp2d_eval as float-or-array and propagated that union into the accumulator.
asi.next_action_hint: Wrap the public interp2d_eval result with float() in the benchmark driver, matching the scalar Numba overload selected at runtime, then rerun baseline.

description: Established the frozen CPU-0-7 baseline for compiled public 1D/2D interpolation workloads; all interpolation, lint, format, and type checks pass.

asi.hypothesis: The corrected broad benchmark provides a valid baseline for pydynopt-only call patterns, including JMP-like repeated scalar 2D field evaluation.

description: Added one-interval upward/downward fast paths to bsearch_impl; large local-query and array gains outweighed a small random-search cost.

asi.hypothesis: The previous lower-bound hint usually differs by at most one interval in model loops, so explicit adjacent-bin checks will avoid binary search.
asi.learning: Adjacent-bin fast paths are highly valuable for local and sequential calls; distant random calls pay for the extra checks, so future search changes should avoid adding more linear probes.

description: Forced all small scalar interpolation helpers inline; performance improved dramatically, but Numba's compiler failed two public 2D path tests with SSA-scope errors.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit always-inlining of tiny scalar helpers will remove dispatcher/helper call overhead in compiled consumer loops.
asi.rollback_reason: Inlining the full helper stack triggered Numba IR/SSA assumption failures in public 2D scalar/array tests; 2 of 63 interpolation tests failed despite a 29% primary timing improvement.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry inlining in smaller subsets to identify a safe boundary, starting with interp1d_eval_scalar and interp2d_eval_scalar only; avoid nesting an always-inlined bsearch inside always-inlined locate initially.
asi.performance_signal: Very strong: interp1d combined fell from about 25-28 ns to 10-13 ns and interp2d combined from about 44-48 ns to 22-24 ns.
asi.numba_failure: NumbaIRAssumptionWarning variables from inlined interp1d_locate_scalar/bsearch_impl not in scope; public 2D scalar path and output-buffer identity tests failed.

description: Revisited run 5 with only 1D/2D evaluation helpers forced inline; checks now pass and the aggregate improves modestly without the nested-search SSA failure.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining only arithmetic evaluation helpers captures call-overhead gains without exposing Numba's nested bsearch SSA bug.
asi.changed_assumption: The failed run conflated six inline decisions; limiting always-inline to leaf evaluation helpers avoids nested inlined control-flow.
asi.learning: Leaf eval helpers are safe to force inline. The gain is small for 2D repeated-field evaluation, implying Numba was already optimizing most of this path, while 1D pipeline and array paths gain more.

description: Revisited run 5 by additionally inlining only fused 1D/2D scalar kernels; public checks pass and combined scalar calls become much faster.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining fused scalar entry kernels, while leaving locate and initial-index helpers at normal inlining policy, will remove the dominant public-overload call boundary safely.
asi.changed_assumption: The Numba SSA failure appears tied to forcing the locate/search helper stack inline, not to inlining fused scalar entry kernels around non-forced locate calls.
asi.combined_1d_effect: Local/random combined cases improved from about 25/28 ns before eval inlining to 13/15 ns.
asi.combined_2d_effect: Local/random combined cases improved from roughly 44/47 ns to 33/37 ns.
asi.learning: The main avoidable overhead was the fused public scalar kernel call boundary; leaf eval plus fused scalar inlining is Numba-safe.

description: Revisited locate inlining with bsearch_impl no longer forced inline; this avoids Numba's nested-inline SSA bug and captures most of the large search-path gain.

asi.hypothesis: Force-inlining locate while leaving bsearch as a normal compiled helper will flatten the public interpolation path without triggering nested-inline SSA corruption.
asi.changed_assumption: The unsafe combination was nested forced inlining of bsearch into locate into 2D kernels; assigning the forced-inline boundary to locate alone is compiler-safe.
asi.learning: This recovered nearly all of run 5's performance while all 63 interpolation tests passed. bsearch's call boundary is cheaper than the locate/public scalar boundaries, and avoids a Numba 0.67/Python 3.14 compiler defect.
asi.max_cv_note: The highest per-case CV rose to 5.6%, but the primary improvement is roughly 15%, far beyond noise.

description: Forced _initial_indices inline; 2D timings improved, but Numba failed to type the dead array-index branch when ilb was None in public array calls.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining the tiny initial-index decoder will remove residual 2D call overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Numba's always-inline pipeline did not eliminate the ilb[0]/ilb[1] branch for a compile-time None argument, causing TypingError in two public 2D tests.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not force-inline the optional-argument helper directly. Consider overload-specific None/array implementations or specialize the public overload only if the added complexity is justified by the roughly 3.5% 2D gain.
asi.performance_signal: 2D locate fell about 40.9 to 38.0 ns and combined local/random about 23.8/26.1 to 21.5/24.1 ns.

description: Changed bilinear evaluation to interpolate along contiguous dimension 1 first, matching the target call pattern; timing was nearly neutral overall and checks failed only because Ruff required formatting.

asi.hypothesis: Evaluating adjacent dimension-1 values before crossing rows will improve address generation and cache locality for C-order 2D arrays.
asi.rollback_reason: Code was semantically valid and tests passed up to the formatting gate, but ruff format --check rejected three line wraps.
asi.next_action_hint: Reapply the arithmetic-order change, run Ruff formatting before benchmarking, and verify whether the 3.6% repeated-eval gain survives while combined-path regressions settle.
asi.performance_signal: C-order repeated-field eval improved from about 6.95 to 6.53 ns and strided eval from 6.90 to 6.82 ns; combined 2D cases appeared 3-4% slower, leaving primary nearly unchanged.

description: Verification of dimension-1-first bilinear arithmetic after formatting; repeated eval improved, but fused 2D scalar paths regressed enough to worsen the aggregate.

asi.hypothesis: Contiguous-dimension-first bilinear evaluation will consistently improve 2D kernels once formatted and fully checked.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 1.8% versus run 8; 2D combined local/random rose from roughly 23.8/26.1 ns to 26.5/32.7 ns despite repeated eval improving about 3.7%.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the original dimension-0-first arithmetic for broad performance. If optimizing repeated eval later, investigate a dedicated code-generation/addressing change that does not alter fused-kernel operation order.
asi.learning: Arithmetic order is specialization-sensitive: the pydynopt eval API benefits from contiguous-first loads, but inlined fused locate+eval code becomes materially worse, especially for random coordinates.

description: Revisited initial-index inlining with compile-time None/indexable overloads; specialization preserves all public paths and removes residual 2D helper overhead.

asi.hypothesis: A type-directed overload can inline separate None and indexable initial-index implementations without exposing invalid dead branches to Numba.
asi.changed_assumption: Instead of forcing the polymorphic helper body inline, the overload generates a branch-free implementation for each compile-time argument type.
asi.learning: Compile-time overload specialization safely recovers the run 9 2D gains: locate improves about 6.8% and combined local about 9.7% versus run 8. 1D variation is noise because its production code is unchanged.
asi.compiler_constraint: Numba overload inline='always' is safe when each generated implementation is type-valid on its own.

description: Rewrote 1D interpolation as upper + weight*(lower-upper); fewer multiplies did not help the compiled pipeline and slightly worsened the aggregate.

asi.hypothesis: Difference-form linear interpolation will reduce arithmetic operations in all 1D evaluate paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.65%; the representative locate-plus-four-evaluations pipeline rose from 8.04 to 8.26 ns, while combined improvements were too small to compensate.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the weighted-sum formulation. Its independent multiplies likely expose more instruction-level parallelism than the shorter dependency chain in difference form.
asi.learning: Operation count alone is misleading for this tiny kernel; dependency depth dominates when several evaluations are accumulated.

description: Forced the allocating/output-buffer 2D scalar locate wrapper inline; Numba already eliminated its boundary and no target workload improved.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining interp2d_locate_scalar will expose supplied buffers, elide optional allocation branches, and remove tuple-return overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.33% and locate2d_local remained essentially unchanged at 38.07 ns versus 38.12 ns; observed variation elsewhere was noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Leave the wrapper at Numba's default policy. Focus on the internal 2D locate implementation or the two search calls rather than wrapper/tuple overhead.
asi.learning: The public overload/wrapper boundary is not the source of the remaining 2D locate cost when output buffers are supplied.

description: Forced the non-allocating 2D scalar locate implementation inline; this removes its real internal call boundary and sharply reduces buffered scalar locate cost.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining interp2d_locate_scalar_impl, rather than its allocation wrapper, will combine initial-index specialization and both searches directly in the wrapper caller.
asi.learning: The internal scalar implementation boundary was costly: locate2d fell from about 38.1 to 26.5 ns. The allocation wrapper itself was not costly in run 14. This distinction should guide remaining array-kernel inlining.

description: Forced combined array loop implementations inline; the aggregate moved only within noise while the directly affected 2D array case regressed materially.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining the non-allocating combined array loops will enable cross-boundary loop optimization similar to the successful scalar 2D locate implementation.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.12% apparent primary improvement is below run-to-run noise and came from unchanged scalar cases; array2d directly regressed about 5.0% (13.75 to 14.44 ns), and grouped array performance regressed about 2.3%.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep combined array loops out of line. Test narrower loop/indexing changes inside the implementations rather than forcing large loops into allocation wrappers.
asi.learning: Inlining benefits tiny straight-line internal implementations, but forcing full array loops increases code size without removing meaningful per-element overhead.

description: Revisited nested bsearch inlining after type-specializing initial indices; compiler checks now pass, but scalar paths do not improve and 2D array code regresses.

asi.hypothesis: With the actual None/indexable inline failure fixed by run 12, restoring bsearch always-inline may safely remove the final search call boundary.
asi.changed_assumption: Run 12 replaced the unsafe polymorphic _initial_indices inlining, allowing a clean test of bsearch inlining by itself.
asi.rollback_reason: Although all checks now pass, primary regressed about 0.45%; scalar timings were unchanged and array2d rose roughly 11% from 13.75 to 15.31 ns due to nested code expansion.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep bsearch_impl at normal inline policy under the forced-inline locate function. The compiler call boundary has no scalar cost and controls array-loop code size.
asi.learning: Run 5's correctness failure was caused by optional initial-index inlining, but its nested bsearch inlining is still undesirable for performance.

description: Forced the public interp1d_eval overload implementation inline into consumers; repeated evaluation slowed, showing the remaining overload call in LLVM is beneficial for code size/scheduling.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining the outer public overload implementation will remove the remaining call visible in compiled benchmark LLVM.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.85%; pipeline1d_4field rose from 8.08 to 8.29 ns and no directly affected case improved.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the public overload boundary. Generated LLVM calls do not imply harmful overhead; leaf/internal inlining already exposes the arithmetic where beneficial.
asi.learning: Inlining across the public overload adds enough code pressure to outweigh a call removal in repeated-field loops.

description: Forced only the public interp1d_locate overload inline; tuple/call overhead disappears in EBL-style locate and locate-plus-multiple-eval loops.

asi.hypothesis: Unlike repeated eval, public locate returns a tuple and carries a search hint, so inlining its outer overload can remove meaningful tuple/call overhead.
asi.learning: Public-overload inlining should be selective: it strongly benefits locate but harmed eval in run 18. EBL's locate-once/evaluate-many pattern now improves directly.

description: Forced the public interp2d_locate overload inline; buffered scalar locate now sheds its outer wrapper/tuple boundary and drops to about 22 ns.

asi.hypothesis: The successful public 1D locate strategy should transfer to 2D locate, where returned buffer tuples cross the same overload boundary.
asi.learning: Selective public locate inlining works in both dimensions. Combined/eval APIs do not inherit this benefit because they use different overload paths; array2d variation is unrelated noise.

description: Forced the public combined 1D overload inline; unlike locate, it did not improve scalar interpolation and enlarged the array path.

asi.hypothesis: Public overload inlining will remove the remaining combined 1D call boundary just as it did for locate.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.4%; directly affected interp1d_local rose from 10.09 to 10.24 ns and array1d from 6.27 to 6.38 ns, with no consistent combined benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep public inlining limited to locate overloads. Fused scalar internals are already inlined enough; forcing the outer combined overload adds code pressure.
asi.learning: Tuple-return/search-hint locate calls are special. The same public-inline policy does not generalize to combined interpolation.

description: Cached lower and upper grid values before computing interpolation weight; this avoids repeated indexed expressions and improves locate-heavy and 2D array paths.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit lower/upper grid locals will help Numba retain loaded endpoints across the weight numerator and denominator.
asi.learning: Numba did not generate equally efficient code from repeated xp[index+1] expressions. Explicit endpoint locals are both clearer and faster. The unchanged eval-only variation is noise.

description: Cached four 2D corner values and the repeated dimension-0 complement in scalar evaluation; repeated-field evaluation improves for both contiguous and strided arrays.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit corner and complement locals will reduce repeated address arithmetic and expose reusable values in the inlined 2D scalar evaluator.
asi.learning: Unlike changing interpolation order, preserving the existing arithmetic tree while naming corner loads/complement improves both C-contiguous and strided repeated-field calls. This is the appropriate optimization pattern for duplicated 2D arithmetic.

description: Applied explicit corner/complement locals to fused 2D scalar interpolation; the optimization did not transfer from eval-only and slightly worsened the aggregate.

asi.hypothesis: The corner-load optimization from run 23 will also improve duplicate bilinear arithmetic in fused 2D scalar interpolation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 1.0%; interp2d_local rose from 21.36 to 21.76 ns, while the random case's small gain did not generalize.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit corners only in interp2d_eval_scalar. In fused code, surrounding search creates different register pressure; do not mechanically duplicate the eval-only optimization.
asi.learning: Identical arithmetic benefits depend on surrounding live values. Fused locate+evaluate has higher register pressure and is hurt by four named corner temporaries.

description: Forced the public 2D eval overload inline; strided-view evaluation benefits strongly, outweighing a modest contiguous-layout regression.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining public 2D eval can scalarize index/weight row views in JMP-like repeated-field callers, unlike scalar-argument 1D eval.
asi.learning: Public 2D eval inlining is layout-sensitive: it substantially improves strided fp[:, 0]-style views while slightly hurting contiguous fp[0]-style views. Both are represented equally, so the grouped result improves about 4.7%.
asi.next_action_hint: Investigate a layout-sensitive inline policy or implementation split to retain the strided gain without the contiguous regression.

description: Tried a layout-sensitive Numba overload inline policy for 2D eval, but Numba 0.67 invokes custom policies with three arguments rather than the two documented in its public docstring.

asi.hypothesis: A custom overload inline policy can inline arbitrary-strided 2D evaluation while keeping C-contiguous evaluation out of line.
asi.rollback_reason: Compilation crashed before measurement: _inline_interp2d_eval() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry the policy with the actual three-argument signature observed in numba.core.typed_passes and inspect those argument structures before selecting fp layout.
asi.numba_version_behavior: Custom inline policy invoked as policy(expr, caller_inline_info, callee_inline_info).

description: Corrected the three-argument layout-sensitive inline policy; desired C/strided timings were achieved, but Numba failed lowering the array-eval output-buffer specialization when the policy returned false.

asi.hypothesis: Inline scalar 2D eval only when fp has arbitrary-strided layout, restoring C-layout performance while retaining the strided gain.
asi.rollback_reason: One public output-buffer test failed: Numba's custom cost-model false path attempted to cast a supplied 1D output array to omitted(default=None) while lowering the index.ndim>1 eval implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry with the policy always returning true for array-index eval paths (index ndim > 1), and layout-selective behavior only for scalar index.ndim == 1. This should avoid Numba's false-path lowering defect for the direct array implementation.
asi.performance_signal: The intended scalar result worked: C eval returned to 6.76 ns and strided stayed near 5.76 ns, grouped 6.24 ns.

description: Retried layout-sensitive 2D eval policy with array paths forced inline; scalar timings and aggregate improved, but Numba's custom inliner hit a folded-argument KeyError on keyword output buffers.

asi.hypothesis: Always inlining index.ndim>1 eval avoids the custom-policy false-path cast bug while preserving layout selection for scalar eval.
asi.changed_assumption: The array path was changed from policy false to true to avoid the prior omitted-output cast.
asi.rollback_reason: Numba still failed the output-buffer specialization, now with KeyError 'iinfo' after custom inliner argument folding for the direct interp2d_eval_array implementation.
asi.next_action_hint: Wrap the array implementation in a generated impl whose full signature/defaults exactly match the overloaded public function before applying the custom policy; direct return of interp2d_eval_array exposes a Numba cost-model bug.
asi.performance_signal: Desired core score reached 10.447 ns; C/strided eval were 6.77/5.76 ns.

description: Retried layout-sensitive 2D eval with a signature-matching array wrapper; cost-model folding progressed, but the nested wrapper could not type the plain allocation function.

asi.hypothesis: A generated array overload implementation matching public defaults will avoid Numba's keyword-output folding bugs while leaving array eval out of line.
asi.changed_assumption: The direct interp2d_eval_array implementation was replaced with a matching nested wrapper so cost-model argument folding sees the public signature.
asi.rollback_reason: Numba could not type the nested wrapper's call to plain interp2d_eval_array; two array-eval public tests failed before lowering.
asi.next_action_hint: Retry by putting the two-line allocation/output-buffer logic directly in the generated implementation and calling the already register_jitable interp2d_eval_array_impl.
asi.performance_signal: Scalar layout policy remains promising: grouped eval 6.228 ns and primary 10.482 ns.

description: Inlined the array allocation logic inside a matching generated overload implementation; Numba still failed the custom cost-model false path for keyword output buffers.

asi.hypothesis: Direct generated allocation logic will make custom-policy argument folding type-correct for array 2D eval.
asi.changed_assumption: The untyped plain wrapper call was removed and replaced by inline allocation plus the registered array kernel.
asi.rollback_reason: The same supplied-output-to-omitted cast failure remained, proving the bug is in Numba's custom cost-model false path with keyword/default folding, not the selected implementation body.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon callable cost models. Register a separate always-inline overload that accepts only scalar index plus A-layout fp, and make the normal overload reject that exact type so each signature has one implementation/policy.
asi.learning: No implementation wrapper can repair this Numba 0.67 custom inliner bug; specialization must occur through separate overload templates.

description: Split 2D eval into a strided scalar always-inline overload and a normal generic overload; this avoids Numba's cost-model bugs and retains both layout-specific strengths.

asi.hypothesis: Separate overload templates with mutually exclusive accepted signatures can express layout-sensitive inlining without a callable Numba cost model.
asi.changed_assumption: The custom cost model was removed entirely; the always-inline template accepts only scalar index plus A-layout fp, while the normal template rejects that signature and handles C/array paths.
asi.learning: Template-level specialization works around Numba 0.67's custom-inliner keyword/default bugs. C evaluation is about 6.77 ns and strided about 5.74 ns, grouped 6.23 ns, with all public output-buffer paths passing.

description: Replaced binary-search branch updates with select-style conditional assignments; random searches did not improve and the aggregate moved backward.

asi.hypothesis: Branchless lower/upper updates will reduce misprediction cost in distant random binary searches while leaving adjacent fast paths untouched.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.22%; locate1d_random stayed near 9.91 ns and interp1d_random worsened from 12.48 to 12.75 ns.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the explicit branch. LLVM may already lower it efficiently, and dual select updates add data dependencies without reducing measured mispredictions.
asi.learning: The random fallback is not improved by source-level branchless assignments.

description: Hoisted .flat iterator objects out of combined array loops; Numba already hoisted equivalent metadata and array performance did not improve.

asi.hypothesis: Caching flat iterators will avoid repeated .flat property construction and shape/stride lookup per array element.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary was effectively unchanged but slightly worse; array1d rose from 6.04 to 6.13 ns and array2d was unchanged around 14.36 ns.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct .flat indexing. To improve arrays, specialize actual memory layouts or reduce per-element interpolation work rather than naming iterator objects.
asi.learning: Numba already optimizes repeated .flat access; explicit flat iterator locals provide no benefit.

description: Split bsearch into an inlined adjacent fast path and out-of-line range fallback; EBL-style locate improved, but fused and array paths regressed, leaving the primary unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining only bsearch's same/adjacent checks while keeping the binary loop out of line will remove calls on local queries without array code expansion.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.013% primary difference is pure noise; although pipeline1d improved about 4%, interp1d_local regressed about 3.1% and grouped arrays regressed about 2.5%, with substantially longer compilation/check time.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain the simpler single bsearch helper. The public 1D locate inlining already captures most model-use performance; splitting search redistributes codegen quality rather than improving it broadly.
asi.learning: Separating hot/cold search paths benefits explicit locate-once pipelines but harms fused and array callers through code layout/pressure.

description: Set NumPy division error semantics on the unchecked locate helper to remove zero-denominator handling; measured improvement was below noise and locate timings were unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: The strict-increasing-grid precondition makes zero-division handling unnecessary, so error_model='numpy' may shorten weight calculation.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.13% primary improvement is below noise; directly affected 1D locate remained 5.64 ns and other changed cases varied inconsistently. The semantic change is not justified without a clear gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain default error semantics. Runtime zero checks are either optimized or correctly predicted and are not a meaningful bottleneck.
asi.learning: Changing Numba's division error model provides no reliable performance benefit for interpolation weights.

description: Cached the repeated dimension-0 complement in the fused 2D array loop; compiler behavior and array timing were unchanged while the aggregate varied negatively.

asi.hypothesis: Naming 1-weight0 once will reduce repeated arithmetic in every 2D array element without the register pressure of four corner locals.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.4%; the directly affected array2d case remained essentially unchanged at 14.38 versus 14.36 ns.
asi.next_action_hint: Do not pursue source-level common-subexpression naming in the array loop; LLVM already performs it. Consider layout specialization or loop structure instead.
asi.learning: The scalar eval gain in run 23 came from explicit corner addressing, not merely naming the repeated weight complement.

description: Reordered explicit 2D corner loads by contiguous rows while preserving the original arithmetic tree; C-layout repeated evaluation improves and strided performance is retained.

asi.hypothesis: Loading each row's adjacent corners together will improve C-layout address generation without the arithmetic-order regression from run 11.
asi.learning: Source load order matters even though the arithmetic tree is unchanged. This recovers contiguous locality while preserving the specialized strided path; unchanged locate variation is noise.
asi.confidence_note: Aggregate gain is diluted because only one of twelve cases changes, but the directly affected C case improves about 2.1% and the code is simpler in memory order.

description: Cached upper 2D corner indices before scalar evaluation; extra live index values hurt the strided specialization and worsened the aggregate.

asi.hypothesis: Precomputing index0+1 and index1+1 will reduce repeated integer address arithmetic for four corner loads.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.46%; strided eval rose from 5.74 to 5.88 ns and C eval also worsened, indicating added register/live-range cost.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep index increments directly in corner subscripts. The backend already folds them into addressing modes.
asi.learning: Explicit grid-value locals help, but explicit upper-index locals prevent efficient address-mode folding or increase register pressure.

description: Cached 1D function endpoints while preserving weighted-sum arithmetic; directly affected 1D paths did not improve, so the tiny aggregate change was unrelated noise.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit lower/upper fp locals may improve 1D evaluation address generation as corner locals did for 2D eval.
asi.rollback_reason: Direct 1D pipeline rose from 6.63 to 6.68 ns and array1d from 6.09 to 6.22 ns; apparent 0.09% primary gain came from unchanged 2D variation.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct fp subscripts in the 1D weighted sum. The 2D corner-local result does not transfer to two-load interpolation.
asi.learning: Explicit value loads only help when several 2D addressing expressions can be simplified; two 1D loads are already optimal.

description: Manually split fused 2D locate into two searches followed by two weight calculations to expose independent divisions; combined paths became slower.

asi.hypothesis: Performing both 2D searches before endpoint loads and weight divisions will expose division-level parallelism hidden by two sequential locate helper calls.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.71%; combined local/random rose from 21.20/23.87 to 22.10/24.60 ns. Extra live search results/endpoints outweighed any division overlap.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep sequential calls to the optimized 1D locate helper. Do not duplicate its logic in fused 2D code.
asi.learning: The backend schedules compact inlined locate calls better than a manually widened two-dimension dataflow.

description: Cached the final valid lower-bound index in bsearch; compiler register allocation shifted but the aggregate did not improve consistently.

asi.hypothesis: Naming n-2 once will reduce repeated integer arithmetic in adjacent upward search checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed slightly; 1D locate was unchanged, combined random paths worsened, and the isolated 2D locate drop was inconsistent with the identical pair of 1D searches and likely code-layout noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Let LLVM common-subexpression elimination handle n-2. Avoid tuning source temporaries to one composite caller's register allocation.
asi.learning: A trivial integer local can redistribute tiny-kernel timings but has no robust broad benefit.

description: Added a C-layout 2D scalar evaluator using one flattened base offset and adjacent corner loads; contiguous repeated-field evaluation nearly halves while strided specialization remains intact.

asi.hypothesis: For compile-time C-contiguous fp, one flat row-major offset will avoid four generic multidimensional address calculations in repeated 2D evaluation.
asi.learning: Layout-specific address generation is the largest remaining 2D eval opportunity. C-layout evaluation drops from about 6.63 to 3.41 ns; A-layout retains its dedicated always-inline path around 5.78 ns.
asi.correctness_guard: The specialized helper is selected only when Numba reports fp.layout == 'C'; F and arbitrary-strided arrays retain generic indexing.

description: Added a C-layout fused 2D scalar kernel using flat row-major offsets; combined local and random interpolation improve while preserving generic-layout behavior.

asi.hypothesis: The flat-offset C-layout optimization from eval-only should reduce the bilinear portion of fused 2D interpolation when selected at overload time.
asi.learning: Compile-time C-layout specialization generalizes to fused scalar interpolation when implemented in its own low-register-pressure kernel. Generic F/A layouts remain on the original implementation.

description: Added a C-layout 2D array kernel with flat offsets; the target array case improved, but widespread unrelated scalar regressions made this run unreliable and the aggregate much worse.

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated C-layout array loop using flat row-major offsets will transfer scalar C specialization gains to each array element.
asi.rollback_reason: Despite array2d improving about 6.2%, primary regressed 5.6% and untouched cases simultaneously regressed: locate2d 41%, combined 11-12%, and several 1D cases 5-7%. Max CV reached 5%, indicating an anomalous run or code-layout effect.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-run the same isolated C-array specialization once to distinguish its strong direct-case gain from system/code-layout noise. Keep only if scalar cases return to normal and aggregate improves.

description: Verification rerun of the C-layout 2D array specialization; unaffected scalar cases normalized, but the target array case no longer improved and the aggregate remained worse.

asi.hypothesis: The strong direct array gain in run 44 will reproduce once the anomalous broad scalar slowdown clears.
asi.changed_assumption: Run 44's unrelated 1D/2D scalar regressions and high CV suggested system noise, so the identical specialization was rerun.
asi.rollback_reason: array2d_local measured 14.87 ns versus 14.55 ns before the change, disproving the apparent 13.64 ns gain from run 44; primary regressed about 0.22%.
asi.next_action_hint: Abandon flat-offset specialization for the fused array loop. Generic multidimensional indexing is already optimal there; scalar C specialization remains valuable.
asi.learning: The confirmation run prevented keeping a noise-driven array optimization.

description: Cached the repeated lower-row complement in the C-layout fused scalar kernel; combined timings changed negligibly and the aggregate worsened.

asi.hypothesis: Explicitly reusing 1-weight0 will further reduce arithmetic in the C-layout fused 2D helper.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.1%; directly affected combined local/random improved only 0.4%/0.2%, below noise, while code complexity increased.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the C fused helper's direct weighted expressions; LLVM already common-subexpressions the complement sufficiently.
asi.learning: The major C-layout gain comes from flat addressing, not source-level complement reuse.

description: Cached fp.flat in the C-layout scalar evaluator; Numba already hoists flat-array metadata and no meaningful eval gain resulted.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing one flat iterator descriptor will reduce repeated metadata construction around four C-layout corner loads.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.45%; C eval changed only from 3.406 to 3.398 ns, far below noise, and no other path is directly affected.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct fp.flat subscripts in tiny C helpers. Numba already canonicalizes the descriptor accesses.
asi.learning: As in run 33, explicit flat iterator caching is not useful even in the specialized scalar helper.

description: Split C-layout fused scalar interpolation into its own always-inline public overload; scalarized hints and flat values reduce combined 2D calls to 17-19 ns.

asi.hypothesis: A mutually exclusive always-inline C-layout combined overload can eliminate caller-side view/call overhead without expanding generic or array implementations.
asi.learning: Unlike globally inlining combined interpolation in run 21, layout-specific template inlining is a major win. Restricting it to scalar C fp controls code size and exposes both flat addressing and hint-row scalarization.
asi.noise_note: Maximum per-case CV was 12%, but directly affected combined gains are 14-17% and the primary improves 2.7%, so the result exceeds noise substantially.

description: Verification rerun of the C-layout combined overload; the 17-19 ns scalar timings reproduced and benchmark dispersion returned to normal.

asi.hypothesis: Run 48's large C-layout combined gains will reproduce despite its high maximum sample CV.
asi.learning: The result is confirmed: interp2d local/random remain 17.34/18.98 ns, and max CV fell from 12.1% to 5.1%. No code changes were needed.

description: Extended always-inline 2D eval overload to C-layout flat evaluator; both C and strided repeated-field paths slowed substantially.

asi.hypothesis: The smaller flat-offset C evaluator may now benefit from outer public-overload inlining and caller-side index/weight view scalarization.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 3.7%; C eval rose from 3.34 to 4.85 ns and strided eval from 5.75 to 5.96 ns. Combined paths remained fast but eval code pressure became severe.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep C eval's public overload out of line and A-layout eval inline only. Flat addressing already delivers the C gain inside the compact callee.
asi.learning: Caller-side scalarization cannot compensate for duplicated flat-eval code in the repeated-field loop; the normal C overload boundary is essential.

description: Added explicit corner/complement locals to the C-layout fused scalar helper; extra live values again hurt combined interpolation.

asi.hypothesis: The C-layout flat helper may gain from the same explicit corner loads that optimized eval-only.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.51%; directly affected combined local/random rose from 17.34/18.98 to 17.48/19.55 ns.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct flat expressions in the fused C helper. Its surrounding searches make corner temporaries costly, consistent with run 24.
asi.learning: Eval-only and fused kernels require distinct expression forms even after C-layout specialization.

description: Fused same/adjacent search and endpoint reuse into the inline 1D locate helper; local, fused, and array workloads improve dramatically, though distant random searches now duplicate fallback checks.

asi.hypothesis: Keeping fast-path grid endpoints live through weight calculation will eliminate the bsearch call and endpoint reloads for same/adjacent intervals.
asi.random_regression: locate1d random +19%, interp1d random +23%, interp2d random +24% because distant fallback re-enters bsearch_impl and repeats local checks.
asi.learning: Endpoint reuse is a major locality optimization and matches the EBL hint-reuse pattern. Next priority is a cold range-search helper that avoids duplicate checks on distant fallbacks without inlining the binary loop.

description: Added a cold range-search helper and routed distant fused-locate fallbacks directly to known bounds; local endpoint reuse remains while random-query duplication is largely removed.

asi.hypothesis: A non-inlined range-only binary helper will preserve fused local endpoints while avoiding repeated same/adjacent checks on distant fallbacks.
asi.changed_assumption: Unlike run 34, the local path now owns and reuses endpoint values through weight calculation; only the cold binary loop is split out, and downward search uses the already-known tighter upper bound.
asi.random_recovery: locate1d random improves from 11.85 to 9.19 ns, interp1d random 15.57 to 13.43 ns, interp2d random 23.60 to 19.43 ns versus run 52.
asi.learning: Hot endpoint-aware locate plus a cold bounded binary helper is the best structure. Random combined 1D remains about 8% above pre-fusion, but broad primary improves another 4.9% while model-local gains remain.

description: Moved cold binary search plus endpoint weighting into one tuple-return helper; call/return overhead severely hurt random paths and even local code layout regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Returning the complete cold locate result will shrink the inlined caller and avoid fallback endpoint reloads.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 5.0%; locate1d random rose from 9.19 to 13.59 ns and interp1d random from 13.43 to 17.08 ns. Local paths also slowed slightly.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the cold helper index-only and calculate/reload endpoints in the inlined caller. Scalar index return ABI is much cheaper than tuple(index, weight).
asi.learning: Cold-path code size is less costly than tuple-return ABI overhead for random searches; run 53's range-only split is optimal.

description: Cached the final interval index in fused locate; tiny aggregate movement hid consistent 1D regressions and inconsistent 2D code-layout gains.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing xp.size-2 in fused hot-path boundary checks and cold upper bounds will reduce repeated shape arithmetic.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.14% primary gain is within noise and directly important 1D paths consistently regressed 2.5-3.7%; 2D improvements were likely caller register-layout effects.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep shape-bound expressions inline and let LLVM fold them per caller. Do not retain a live last-index value through the hot path.
asi.learning: As in run 41, explicit final-index locals destabilize register allocation rather than robustly reducing work.

description: Specialized public 2D locate when both output buffers are supplied; optional branches were already eliminated and the direct gain was below noise.

asi.hypothesis: A branch-free generated overload implementation for supplied index/weight buffers will reduce 2D locate wrapper overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.16%; locate2d changed only from 14.65 to 14.47 ns, below noise, while the overload gained substantial duplicated code.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the shared allocation wrapper. Numba already folds its optional-output branches for concrete buffer types.
asi.learning: The remaining buffered 2D locate cost is not optional-buffer dispatch.

description: Rewrote fused locate as early-return same/up/down/fallback paths; removing SSA merges improves every 1D case, random 2D, and arrays while retaining endpoint reuse.

asi.hypothesis: Early returns with branch-local endpoint names will eliminate Numba SSA phi complexity and improve code generation for the always-inlined locate helper.
asi.learning: SSA-friendly source structure is critical under Numba always-inlining. Branch-local returns outperform merged index/lower/upper state and are expected to reduce NumbaIRAssumptionWarnings; local 2D combined needs separate investigation.

description: Stopped forcing the C-layout fused scalar helper inline after its locate body grew; the resulting helper call more than doubled combined 2D overhead.

asi.hypothesis: Keeping the larger SSA-friendly locate body out of the caller may reduce code pressure and recover local 2D combined performance.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 11.8%; combined local/random jumped from 11.9/15.9 to 26.6/26.9 ns. The call boundary dominates despite larger inline code.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep _interp2d_scalar_c forced inline. Investigate its local regression through branch ordering or caller structure, not by restoring a helper call.
asi.learning: The C fused kernel must remain fully inline; its flat addressing and searches need cross-boundary scalarization.

description: Located contiguous/fast-moving dimension 1 before dimension 0 in the C-layout fused scalar kernel; local combined calls improve with a small random-case tradeoff.

asi.hypothesis: In the JMP-like C-layout call pattern, searching the large fast-moving contiguous dimension before the small slow-moving dimension will improve instruction/branch scheduling.
asi.learning: Search order matters in fully inlined C-layout combined code. Dimension 1 first favors the representative local pattern and improves the balanced primary; generic-layout and separate locate APIs retain dimension-0-first order.

description: Reordered searches in the buffered 2D locate implementation; unlike fused C interpolation, dimension 1 first worsened standalone locate.

asi.hypothesis: Dimension-1-first search order from run 59 will also benefit standalone buffered 2D locate.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.69%; directly affected locate2d rose from 13.63 to 14.01 ns. The benefit is specific to fused C-layout scheduling, not search alone.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep standalone 2D locate dimension 0 first. Do not generalize run 59's order to other kernels.
asi.learning: Search ordering interacts with subsequent flat bilinear arithmetic; without that arithmetic, original dimension order is faster.

description: Reordered searches in fused 2D array interpolation; the target array case improved, but unrelated scalar noise left the primary worse.

asi.hypothesis: Searching fast-moving dimension 1 first inside the fused array loop will improve its per-element scheduling.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.41% despite array2d improving 4.3% from 8.14 to 7.79 ns; unchanged scalar/random cases supplied the opposing movement.
asi.next_action_hint: Re-run this one-line ordering change once because the directly affected signal is strong and expected aggregate effect is only about 0.36%, easily hidden by suite noise.

description: Verification of dimension-1-first fused array search reproduced the array gain, but the balanced primary again failed to improve.

asi.hypothesis: The direct 4.3% array2d improvement from run 61 will translate to an aggregate gain on confirmation.
asi.changed_assumption: Run 61's unchanged scalar movement could have hidden the expected roughly 0.36% primary benefit, so the identical change was repeated.
asi.rollback_reason: array2d reproduced at 7.80 ns, but primary again regressed, now about 0.64%; two runs did not satisfy the frozen balanced acceptance metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain dimension-0-first array order despite the isolated benchmark signal. Do not tune further to this single case.
asi.learning: The direct array effect is real but too narrow to improve the balanced suite reliably, so keeping it would overfit one workload.

description: Restored NaN hint semantics by retaining the original lower-search upper bound; the simpler bound also improves scalar locate performance and the primary metric.

asi.hypothesis: Using the original hint as the downward binary-search upper bound preserves unordered-NaN behavior and may compile more efficiently than the tightened index-minus-one bound.
asi.semantic_fix: For NaN with ilb>=2, index-1 was not a proven upper bound because comparisons are unordered; it returned one interval below the Python/bsearch path. Added compiled-vs-Python regression coverage.
asi.tradeoff: interp1d_random rose about 2.1% and array1d about 2.5%, while scalar locate and aggregate improved.
asi.learning: A mathematically tighter bound for ordered values was invalid for NaN and generated worse code. Preserve the original search bound.

description: Hoisted the extrapolation mode outside the 1D array loop and added a direct extrapolating loop; array interpolation avoids a per-element mode branch and improves about 5%.

asi.hypothesis: A dedicated extrapolating 1D array loop will hoist the invariant mode branch and expose direct interpolation arithmetic, avoiding per-element helper control flow.
asi.learning: LLVM did not fully recover the optimal extrapolate=True array loop through the shared evaluator; source-level loop versioning gives a narrow but reproducible direct-path gain.

description: Hoisted extrapolation mode outside the 2D array loop and added a direct extrapolating loop; array2d improves about 7% and the primary metric falls further.

asi.hypothesis: The successful 1D array loop versioning from run 64 will transfer to 2D, removing invariant extrapolation control flow from every element.
asi.learning: Source-level extrapolation loop versioning benefits both 1D and 2D arrays; the larger 2D loop sees an even stronger direct gain.

description: Loaded extrapolating 2D array corners in contiguous row order before bilinear arithmetic; array2d and the primary metric improve further.

asi.hypothesis: After loop versioning, explicit row-contiguous corner loads in the extrapolating 2D array loop will reduce multidimensional address scheduling overhead.
asi.changed_assumption: Earlier fused scalar corner locals suffered register pressure, but the versioned array loop has no extrapolation condition and amortizes stable row-wise load scheduling.
asi.learning: The row-order corner-load optimization transfers to the dedicated extrapolating array loop, though its gain is smaller than in eval-only scalar code.

description: Cached the dimension-0 complement in the versioned 2D array loop; added live state hurt array and aggregate performance.

asi.hypothesis: Explicitly reusing 1-weight0 after row-ordered corner loads will remove duplicate subtraction in the extrapolating 2D array loop.
asi.changed_assumption: The loop is now versioned and corners are explicitly loaded row-wise, so complement reuse could have become visible to code generation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 1.44% and array2d rose from 7.49 to 7.66 ns; LLVM already eliminates or schedules the duplicate expression better than the extra source local.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct complement expressions in the versioned array loop; do not add more arithmetic temporaries.

description: Named 1D array value endpoints before weighted evaluation; direct loads already compiled optimally and the aggregate regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit fp endpoint locals in the dedicated extrapolating 1D array loop will improve load scheduling after loop versioning.
asi.changed_assumption: The change was limited to the newly versioned extrapolating array loop rather than the shared scalar evaluator.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed about 0.9% and array1d stayed effectively unchanged at 3.71 ns; explicit endpoint names provide no direct benefit.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct fp subscripts in the 1D array loop; pursue loop-level rather than load-naming changes.

description: Retried flat row-major corner offsets inside the versioned 2D array loop; array2d improved narrowly, but the balanced primary did not.

asi.hypothesis: With early-return locate, loop versioning, and row-wise corner locals, flat offsets may now transfer the scalar C-layout addressing gain to array2d.
asi.changed_assumption: The array loop has since shed extrapolation control flow and materially lower search/register pressure.
asi.rollback_reason: array2d improved from 7.49 to 7.36 ns, but primary regressed 0.19%; the narrow gain again failed balanced acceptance.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain multidimensional row-ordered loads. Do not retry flat array offsets.

description: Split cold binary search into upward and downward three-argument helpers; the aggregate moved only within noise and direct search cases did not consistently improve.

asi.hypothesis: Directional cold search helpers will remove one bound argument and specialize a constant bound for distant queries.
asi.rollback_reason: The apparent 0.08% primary gain is below noise; locate1d random worsened slightly and array workloads regressed, while duplicated helper code increased complexity.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the single four-argument _bsearch_range helper. Call ABI bound specialization is not a useful bottleneck.

description: Cached lower and upper row views in the generic 2D scalar evaluator; arbitrary-strided repeated-field evaluation improves about 4%.

asi.hypothesis: Caching two row views will reuse dimension-0 base address calculations across adjacent dimension-1 corner loads for arbitrary-strided values.
asi.learning: For arbitrary-strided 2D arrays, row-view base caching is better than four independent multidimensional addresses; C-layout still uses its flat-offset specialization.

description: Applied row-view base caching to the extrapolating 2D array loop; array interpolation and the primary metric improve modestly.

asi.hypothesis: The row-view address reuse that improved arbitrary-strided scalar evaluation will also reduce repeated dimension-0 address setup in the versioned 2D array loop.
asi.learning: Row base reuse transfers to array interpolation and remains useful alongside compile-time C-layout optimization, with a smaller gain than eval-only.

description: Forced the cold range-only binary helper inline after the early-return rewrite; random 1D improved, but code expansion hurt arrays and random 2D.

asi.hypothesis: The smaller range-only helper and branch-local locate structure may now make binary-loop inlining profitable for distant searches.
asi.changed_assumption: The inlined helper no longer contains same/adjacent checks, and the caller now uses early returns without SSA merges.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.29%; array1d worsened 6.8% and random2d 1.8%, despite locate1d random improving 3.1%. Compilation also expanded materially.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the binary range loop out of line. Its call cost is preferable to duplicated code in array and 2D callers.

description: Used an explicit right shift for binary-search midpoints; LLVM already optimizes nonnegative floor division and the apparent aggregate change was noise.

asi.hypothesis: Because search bounds are nonnegative, an explicit right shift may generate a shorter midpoint calculation than floor division by two.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary improved only 0.056%, below noise; directly affected random locate changed by just 0.01 ns and arrays worsened.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep // 2 for clarity; LLVM already strength-reduces it.

description: Changed the cold binary loop condition to an interval-width subtraction; 1D random improved, but 2D combined paths regressed and the primary gain was below noise.

asi.hypothesis: Comparing the binary interval width to one may shorten loop control and aid distant searches.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.038% primary gain is noise; interp2d local/random worsened about 2.3% while locate1d random improved 2.3%, so the change is not broadly beneficial.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the existing upper-versus-lower-plus-one condition.

description: Retried dimension-1-first search only in the versioned extrapolating 2D array loop; the prior direct gain disappeared after row-view caching.

asi.hypothesis: After loop versioning and row-base caching, dimension-1-first search may finally improve both array2d and the balanced primary.
asi.changed_assumption: Only the extrapolating loop is reordered, and its value addressing now uses cached row views.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.81% and array2d itself worsened from 7.49 to 7.62 ns; the changed loop structure invalidated the earlier isolated gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep dimension 0 first in both 2D array branches.

description: Loaded generic 2D scalar indices before weights to expose fp address dependencies earlier; the strided signal was small and the primary regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Loading indices before weights will start dependent row-address calculation earlier in repeated 2D evaluation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.25%; strided eval moved only about 1.1% and unchanged workloads dominated the opposite direction.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep weights first so non-extrapolating rejection can avoid index/address work and source order remains semantically efficient.

description: Removed the explicit shared dimension-0 complement from generic 2D evaluation; strided repeated-field evaluation regressed materially.

asi.hypothesis: With cached row views, spelling 1-weight0 twice may let LLVM schedule arithmetic without an explicit live complement local.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.59% and strided eval rose from about 5.69 to 5.89 ns; explicit complement reuse is important in this tiny evaluator.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve upper_weight0 in scalar 2D evaluation and document it as intentional.

description: Inlined only C-eval index/weight extraction and called a non-inline scalar-components helper; call ABI changes did not improve C evaluation.

asi.hypothesis: A tiny inline wrapper can scalarize index/weight views while keeping C bilinear arithmetic out of line, avoiding run 50's code-pressure failure.
asi.changed_assumption: Unlike run 50, only four component loads are inlined; flat corner loads and arithmetic remain in a compact callee.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.03% primary movement is noise and C eval regressed from about 3.34 to 3.40 ns; passing six scalar/array arguments is no cheaper than passing two row views.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the compact out-of-line C eval overload with its internal always-inline flat helper.

description: Named C-eval index components before flat offset calculation; extra source locals did not aid addressing and the aggregate regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Explicit index0/index1 locals may expose scalar view loads and shorten C flat-offset address calculation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.35% and C eval stayed around 3.40 ns; each component is used once and LLVM already loads it optimally.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the compact offset expression.

description: Added a scalar-only always-inline public 1D interpolation overload while leaving arrays out of line; combined scalar calls improve 9-16%.

asi.hypothesis: After the branch-local locate rewrite, a mutually exclusive scalar-only public overload can remove combined-call overhead without expanding array code.
asi.changed_assumption: Run 21 forced one shared overload policy before early-return locate and also exposed the array path; the new template inlines only scalar signatures and leaves arrays on the normal overload.
asi.learning: Public combined 1D inlining becomes strongly profitable when isolated from array signatures and paired with SSA-friendly locate code.

description: Retried scalar-only public 1D eval inlining after the locate rewrite; repeated-field pipeline performance again regressed.

asi.hypothesis: SSA-friendly locate and scalar-only overload isolation may now make public eval inlining profitable in locate-plus-four-field callers.
asi.changed_assumption: The caller's locate body and overload organization changed substantially, and array eval signatures remain on a normal overload.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.26% and pipeline1d rose 3.3% from 5.15 to 5.32 ns, confirming that the eval call boundary still aids scheduling/code size.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep public 1D eval out of line even though public combined 1D interpolation is now inline.

description: Loaded the C-layout row length before both searches in fused 2D interpolation; longer live range outweighed any latency overlap.

asi.hypothesis: Loading fp.shape[1] before searches may overlap metadata access and shorten the post-search flat-address critical path.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.50%; local combined2d improved only 1.2% while random combined2d worsened about 1%, and unrelated code layout degraded.
asi.next_action_hint: Load n1 immediately before flat offset calculation to avoid retaining it across both searches.

description: Cached the upper-row flat offset in C scalar evaluation; LLVM already folded repeated address additions and C eval worsened.

asi.hypothesis: Reusing offset+n1 for two upper-row corner loads will reduce integer address arithmetic in C evaluation.
asi.rollback_reason: The 0.09% primary gain is below noise and C eval rose from roughly 3.34-3.38 to 3.40 ns; the apparent gain came from unrelated cases.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct flat offset expressions; backend addressing already shares the row displacement.

description: Retried explicit complement reuse in the C fused scalar helper after locate restructuring; direct gains remained too small to improve the balanced primary.

asi.hypothesis: Branch-local locate and scalar-only public inlining may now make one shared 1-weight0 value profitable in fused C interpolation.
asi.changed_assumption: The surrounding locate SSA and public overload code changed substantially since the first test.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.05%; combined local/random improved only 0.7%/0.6%, again too narrow and small to offset register/code-layout effects.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain direct complement expressions in fused C interpolation; two runs show no balanced benefit.

description: Added an array-only always-inline public 1D overload to remove one wrapper boundary; code expansion destabilized the compiled suite and broadly regressed performance.

asi.hypothesis: Inlining only the allocation/output wrapper while retaining the array loop implementation call will remove one array call boundary safely.
asi.changed_assumption: The scalar overload is now separate and array loops are versioned, unlike the shared public inlining tested in run 21.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 9.3%; array1d rose 18%, array2d 15%, and many scalar/search paths also slowed. Extra array overload inlining causes severe code-layout/compiler effects.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep all public array overloads at default inline policy; do not apply the analogous change to 2D.

description: Retried complement caching in the row-view 2D array loop; the target case was unchanged, so the apparent primary gain came from unrelated noise.

asi.hypothesis: Row-view address caching may free enough registers for explicit 1-weight0 reuse to benefit the 2D array loop.
asi.changed_assumption: Corner addressing now keeps only two row bases rather than four multidimensional address expressions.
asi.rollback_reason: array2d changed only from 7.487 to 7.473 ns, far below noise; the 0.32% aggregate gain came from untouched scalar cases and does not justify the extra local.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep direct complement expressions in array2d and rely on LLVM CSE.

description: Shortened the upper-row view live range by loading the lower row first; serializing row setup hurt strided evaluation.

asi.hypothesis: Loading both lower-row corners before creating the upper-row view will reduce live descriptors and register pressure.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.20% and strided eval rose about 3% to 5.75 ns; constructing both row bases first exposes more memory-level parallelism.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve lower-row/upper-row setup before all four corner loads, and document the ordering.

description: Moved generic 2D complement calculation ahead of corner loads to overlap arithmetic; compiler scheduling and eval performance were unchanged.

asi.hypothesis: Computing 1-weight0 before dependent row loads will hide its latency behind corner memory accesses.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary was unchanged/slightly worse and strided eval stayed at 5.58 ns; LLVM already schedules the independent subtraction appropriately.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep complement calculation adjacent to bilinear arithmetic for clearer source.

description: Reversed hot upper-bound comparison operands without changing semantics; generated performance did not improve and 2D paths regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Writing x < upper may produce a more favorable compare/branch form than upper > x in hot same/adjacent paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.60%; 1D locate was unchanged and 2D locate/array worsened, so operand spelling provides no backend gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep upper > x, which reads naturally as the bracketing condition.

description: No-change verification of run 81/72 best; most scalar results reproduced, while array2d showed a transient slowdown and raised the aggregate.

asi.hypothesis: The current best source will reproduce near 7.00 ns without code changes.
asi.rollback_reason: The rerun measured 7.08 ns due mainly to array2d at 8.30 versus 7.49 ns; no source change exists to keep, and stable scalar cases stayed close.
asi.next_action_hint: Treat array2d as the largest remaining run-level noise source; use the best kept source and additional end-of-run verification rather than reacting to one transient.

description: Cached ilb1+1 for the two upper-column row-view loads in array2d; backend addressing already folds the increment and no target gain resulted.

asi.hypothesis: A shared next-column index will remove duplicate integer increments in row-view corner loads.
asi.changed_assumption: The target is now the versioned row-view array loop rather than scalar multidimensional indexing.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.28% and array2d was unchanged/slightly worse at 7.51 ns; the increment is already folded into addressing modes.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep ilb1+1 directly in each row subscript.

description: Reversed cold binary-loop comparison orientation; results were indistinguishable from the existing condition and the tiny primary movement was noise.

asi.hypothesis: Writing lower-plus-one less-than upper may produce a more favorable loop branch orientation.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary improved only 0.064%; random locate was unchanged and no directly affected case showed a meaningful gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the established upper-greater-than-lower-plus-one spelling.

description: Used xp.size for 1D grid bounds instead of shape[0]; Numba's size access generated worse hot-path code.

asi.hypothesis: For one-dimensional grids, xp.size may provide a cheaper scalar bound than indexing shape[0].
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.67% and local locate rose 3.3% from about 3.46 to 3.58 ns; shape[0] is the better Numba metadata path.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve xp.shape[0] in all hot locate bounds.

description: Expressed final-interval checks as index+2 == shape; 1D random improved but 2D callers suffered severe code-generation regressions.

asi.hypothesis: Comparing index+2 with grid length may avoid subtracting two from shape metadata on upward paths.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.72%; locate2d rose 5.7% and interp2d local 11%, despite a strong but isolated interp1d-random gain.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep index == shape[0]-2; its inlined code composes much better in 2D callers.

description: Second no-change verification of the current best source; 2D and array timings reproduced while 1D locate/pipeline showed transient slowdown.

asi.hypothesis: The run-81 source should remain near its 7.00 ns best across verification measurements.
asi.rollback_reason: No source change exists; this run measured 7.04 ns due 1D locate/pipeline variation, while most cases remained close.
asi.next_action_hint: Retain run 81 as best; perform one final no-change measurement at run 100 after documentation/comments are prepared.

description: Created the upper row view before the lower row in generic 2D evaluation; strided access regressed sharply.

asi.hypothesis: Preparing the upper row base first may overlap its index increment with lower-row setup.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.57% and strided eval rose about 8.6% to 6.06 ns; lower-row-first descriptor creation is essential for current scheduling.
asi.next_action_hint: Document exact lower-row then upper-row setup and contiguous lower/upper corner load order.

description: Stored 2D locate weights before indices to shorten floating-value live ranges; buffered locate slowed substantially.

asi.hypothesis: Writing weight results first will release floating registers before integer output stores in 2D locate.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.19% and locate2d rose 4.5% from about 13.7 to 14.34 ns; contiguous index stores first schedule better.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve index_out[0:2] stores before weight_out[0:2], and document the ordering.

description: Pre-final no-change verification reproduced the current source at 7.00 ns with stable workload timings.

asi.hypothesis: The selected run-81 source will reproduce its approximately 7.00 ns aggregate before the final run.
asi.rollback_reason: No source change exists; 7.0019 ns is 0.08% above the kept 6.9964 ns best and confirms it within noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Use run 100 as the final no-change measurement, then stop experiments and add documentation/comments.

description: Final no-change verification at the 100-run limit reproduced the selected source and set the best measured aggregate at 6.98 ns.

asi.hypothesis: The selected source will reproduce near 7.00 ns in the final run and provide the settled measurement.
asi.termination: Reached the user-requested total of 100 experiments; no further run_experiment calls will be made.
asi.learning: Final stable timings confirm the run-81 source plus earlier kept array/eval improvements. The no-change measurement improved the recorded best by 0.21% to 6.9816 ns.

description: Retried explicit C fused corner locals after the branch-local locate rewrite; added live values still hurt combined interpolation and broader code layout.

asi.hypothesis: With branch-local locate lifetimes, explicit contiguous-row corner loads may now improve the C-layout fused scalar kernel.
asi.changed_assumption: The two inlined locate calls now use early returns and substantially shorter branch-local endpoint lifetimes than in run 51.

description: No-change verification with the final comments and performance guide reproduced the selected implementation near 6.99 ns.

asi.hypothesis: The documented final implementation should reproduce the 6.98 ns best without any source-code optimization change.

description: Tightened the upward cold-search lower bound using the already-proven next grid point; despite a valid invariant, generated search/caller performance regressed broadly.

asi.hypothesis: After next_upper <= x, starting cold search at next_index+1 will narrow the range and avoid considering one impossible interval.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 2.4%; locate1d random rose about 11%, local locate 4%, and local 2D combined about 11%, despite the mathematically tighter bound.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep next_index as the fallback lower bound. Binary iteration shape and inlined caller code generation outweigh the one-element range tightening.
asi.learning: A stronger search invariant is not automatically faster; midpoint sequence and caller register/code layout dominate this tiny kernel.

description: Reversed operand order in the cold binary comparison while preserving NaN semantics; generated performance was indistinguishable from the current form.

asi.hypothesis: Writing needle < haystack[mid] may generate a more favorable compare orientation in distant binary searches.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary was 0.019% worse; random locate and combined random 1D were unchanged/slightly slower, so the forms are equivalent within noise.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep haystack[mid] > needle for readability and consistency with the standalone search.

description: Removed explicit 2D array corner locals while retaining row views; losing the tested row-contiguous load schedule slowed array2d materially.

asi.hypothesis: Row-base caching may make four explicit corner locals unnecessary and reduce register pressure in the versioned 2D array loop.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.80% and array2d rose 4.3% from about 7.46 to 7.78 ns; direct expressions restore column-wise dependency scheduling.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit lower0/lower1/upper0/upper1 locals and their row-contiguous load order, as documented.

description: Revisited branchless binary bound updates in the cold range helper; isolated random locate improved, but composed pipelines, arrays, and 2D callers regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Select-style bound updates may reduce unpredictable branches now that only distant fallbacks execute the isolated range helper.
asi.changed_assumption: The branchless loop is confined to the non-inlined cold range helper rather than the former full search implementation with adjacent checks.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.086%; locate1d random improved 3.1%, but pipeline1d, combined random, arrays, and 2D callers moved backward.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep explicit binary branches for balanced composition; do not specialize solely for isolated random locate.
asi.learning: Branchless search can win in isolation but worsens instruction dependencies and caller composition enough to lose the balanced metric.

description: Inverted 1D array loop versioning so the common extrapolating loop falls through; array1d improved narrowly but the balanced primary did not.

asi.hypothesis: Placing the non-extrapolating loop behind the taken branch will make the common extrapolate=True loop the fall-through path.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary was 0.043% worse; array1d improved about 1.1%, but the effect was too narrow and unchanged 2D cases moved backward.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the established extrapolating-loop-first structure; do not tune branch layout to one narrow case.

description: Inverted 2D array loop versioning so extrapolation falls through; unlike 1D, the larger row-cached loop compiled worse in that position.

asi.hypothesis: Making the common extrapolate=True 2D array loop the fall-through path may reduce mode-branch overhead.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.32% and array2d rose 2.3% from about 7.46 to 7.63 ns; source block order affects the larger loop negatively.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the extrapolating 2D loop first with its early return, as documented.

description: Loaded the hinted upper endpoint before the lower endpoint to expose both memory operations earlier; delaying the first comparison dependency hurt hot locate paths.

asi.hypothesis: Loading the upper endpoint first may overlap adjacent grid loads and shorten the later upper-bound comparison path.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.85%; local locate rose 2.2%, array1d 2%, and combined/random 2D also worsened.
asi.next_action_hint: Preserve lower-then-upper endpoint load order because the first direction comparison depends on lower.

description: Reversed the initial lower-bound comparison operands while preserving NaN behavior; 1D locate was unchanged and array2d/code layout regressed.

asi.hypothesis: Writing x >= lower may produce a more favorable hot direction compare than lower <= x.
asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 0.66%; locate1d was unchanged while array2d rose about 6%, showing no direct backend benefit and adverse code layout.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep lower <= x for consistent grid-first comparisons.

description: Added a dimension-1-first hint extraction overload for fused C interpolation; duplicated overload machinery worsened C callers and code layout.

asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 1.3%; combined2d local/random rose about 4.8%/1.6%, and locate/array2d also worsened. Extra overload/code structure dominates any load ordering.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the shared _initial_indices overload and let LLVM schedule tuple component loads; only reorder the actual C searches.

description: Peeled the first cold binary-search iteration to remove one loop test; LLVM's existing loop form was better and search paths regressed.

asi.rollback_reason: Primary regressed 1.7%; locate1d local/random rose about 12%/6%, and combined 1D local also worsened.
asi.next_action_hint: Keep the canonical while loop; LLVM already rotates/optimizes it more effectively than source duplication.

description: Calculated the C-eval flat offset before loading weights to expose its dependency chain earlier; C evaluation was unchanged and the primary did not improve.

description: Moved the shared C-eval complement ahead of four corner loads; C evaluation improved, but the balanced primary remained slightly worse.

asi.hypothesis: Computing 1-weight0 before C-layout corner loads may overlap the subtraction with memory latency while preserving row-contiguous loads.

asi.learning: Moving only the complement, without disturbing contiguous corner loads, may reduce C-layout eval latency; this is the strongest isolated signal among recent source-order experiments.
